en: Now what's the time complexity of our linked
list-based priority queue?
Let's have a look at the code. When we
insert a new item,
we of course could have constant time
complexity if we don't have a first item yet
or if the priority of the to-be-inserted
item is higher than the existing first
item's priority.
Then we don't need to go through the linked
list. Instead, we just overwrite the first
item and that has constant time.
But this is of course just the best case.
We're not always going to add items with the
highest priority.
By the way, if we are,
a stack might be better because there you
always process the last item you just added.
Instead, we're probably sometimes going to
add items with a high priority and we're
sometimes going to add items
with a low priority. Hence, we'll often make
it into the else case and there we'll often
walk through the entire list or at least
large chunks of our list.
Hence, the time complexity for inserting
items is O in the worst case. It's of course
O in the best case if it's the first item or
an item with the highest priority. But worst
case is O.
Now what about processing?
Well, we always process the first item, so
we'll never need to walk through our linked
list there,
and hence processing of course is super
efficient.
Processing in our linked list-based priority
queue is always O.
So this is not bad. Linear time for
inserting,
Constant time for processing and sometimes
also constant time for inserting is
definitely not horrible. But of course, it
might also not be ideal,
especially if we maybe can do better. And
you might already guess it, we can do
better.
